title: KV memory tiering experiments — PCIe/UMA policy notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This note captures a set of small-scale experiments and the proposed runtime policy for tiering KV-cache residency across: (1) GPU local (GPU DRAM), (2) host pinned/UMA (page pinned to avoid copy for systems where UMA or fast CPU<->GPU mapping exists), and (3) host pageable with PCIe DMA on demand. Goal: reduce out-of-memory events and tail latency regressions under peak throughput while minimizing PCIe bandwidth costs and CPU memory pressure.

Why we need a three-tier policy:
- Increasing model sizes and larger context windows lead to KV working sets that often exceed GPU RAM. Simple wholesale eviction to host pageable memory causes high tail latency on cold misses (DMA ping-pong) and overloads PCIe.
- UMA or zero-copy mappings can be an intermediate tradeoff: lower latency than pageable + DMA for frequently re-used KV pages but consumes host pinned memory and increases GC pressure on host.
- A policy that adapts placement based on access frequency, recency, and PCIe bandwidth availability gives predictable tail SLOs and keeps unit cost manageable.

Key definitions and knobs (vocab):
- hot_residency_min_ms: minimum observed in-GPU residency time to be considered 'hot' (default 50 ms)
- access_freq_score: EWMA of accesses per second per KV shard
- pinned_fraction_target: target percent of working set we allow to remain in host pinned pages (default 10%)
- dma_max_outstanding: limit on concurrent PCIe DMA transfers (default 32)
- prefetch_window_tokens: token lookahead used to prefetch adjacent KV blocks (default 256 tokens)
- cold_eviction_age_ms: age threshold since last access to move GPUs->host-pageable (default 5000 ms)

Placement policy (high level):
1) Admission: new KV pages created on GPU when capacity allows. If GPU memory is constrained, decide target tier based on a quick heuristic: recent-access history + model-usage priority (pinned if high reuse expected).
2) Promotion: host-pageable -> host-pinned when access_freq_score exceeds promotion_threshold. This operation pins host memory (mlock or numa-aware pin) and optionally sets up a zero-copy mapping if hardware/driver allows. Promotion has a small CPU cost; we batch promotions to amortize syscalls.
3) Direct DMA fetch: if page is in host-pageable and requested, we issue a DMA transfer into GPU staging buffer and insert into GPU cache. DMA is limited by dma_max_outstanding and a bandwidth cap. On heavy load, we deliberately delay low-priority DMA (see backpressure).
4) Demotion: pages unused for > cold_eviction_age_ms move GPU->host-pinned if pinned_fraction_target not exceeded, else move GPU->host-pageable (free pinned slots).

Prefetching heuristics:
- For chat-like left-to-right workloads: prefetch next N KV blocks where N determined by prefetch_window_tokens and observed stride.
- For generation batches with similar prefixes: detect common prefix fingerprints and bulk-prefetch matching KV ranges.
- Use a probabilistic prefetch budget: at most X% of dma bandwidth is allowed for prefetch; excess prefetch dropped.

PCIe / UMA tradeoff numeric assumptions (experiment parameters):
- PCIe Gen4 observed ~12–16 GB/s, overhead per DMA setup ~20–50 us depending on transfer size and driver. For small KV blocks (~64 KiB) overhead dominates.
- UMA/zero-copy average access latency observed ~2–6x slower than GPU-local memory for random access, but ~5–10x faster than PCIe DMA cold-miss roundtrip for small accesses.
- Host pinned memory has cost: increased page fault overhead for OS and higher memory pressure affecting other processes (noted in multi-tenant machines).

Backpressure and QoS rules:
- If dma_outstanding >= dma_max_outstanding or measured dma_bandwidth > dma_bandwidth_limit_mib, move low-priority requests to fallback model variant or enqueue them with a soft deadline.
- For requests with strict latency SLOs (configured per-route), prefer serving from pinned pages; if pinned unavailable then proactively fail fast with a graceful error code so application can retry or fallback.
- Meter PCIe bandwidth per-tenant and deny prefetch beyond budget.

Observability (metrics to add):
- kv.hot_hit_rate, kv.pinned_hit_rate, kv.pageable_hit_rate (percentages)
- kv.pinned_bytes, kv.pageable_bytes, kv.gpu_bytes
- dma.outstanding, dma.avg_latency_us, dma.bandwidth_mib_s
- eviction.rate_per_min, demotion.count, promotion.count
- tail_latency_p99_per_route when DMA happened vs no-DMA

Microbench experiment plan (minimal reproducible tests):
1) Synthetic random-access trace: generate uniform and Zipfian access patterns across a fixed working set of KV pages to measure hit-rates and DMA pressure. Vary pinned_fraction_target and record p99 latency and total PCIe bytes transferred.
2) Prefix-batching trace: simulate 1000 concurrent sessions with similar prompt prefixes to measure prefetching efficiency and pinned promotion benefits.
3) Production replay: sample anonymized recent traffic (strip user data) for a single high-traffic route and replay to staging cluster with flags toggled.

Preliminary results (small cluster run Jan 2025):
- Uniform random with working_set=12GB, gpu_ram=8GB: baseline (evict to pageable) p99 = 480ms; pinned_fraction_target=12% reduced p99 to 230ms while increasing host pinned bytes by ~1.4GB and PCIe bytes dropped by 42%.
- Zipfian hot=5%: with promotion thresholds tuned, pinned promotion produced hit rates >85% and DMA bandwidth <25% of baseline.
- Prefetching: naive aggressive prefetch increased PCIe usage by 70% with only marginal hit improvements; bounded prefetch budget (10% BW) recovered most benefit with limited cost.

Implementation notes and low-level mechanics:
- Use asynchronous PCIe DMA engine via our existing host DMA queue. Each transfer gets a small completion callback which updates the access_freq_score. Batch smaller KV blocks into larger contiguous DMA ops where physical layout allows (reduces per-transfer overhead).
- Pinning implemented via madvise/MLock on Linux; ensure we coordinate with container memory limits and cgroups. Provide a guardrail: do not exceed pinned_fraction_target or the process OOM score threshold.
- Integrate with existing KV placement metadata (shard-level residency + epoch counters) to avoid races during migration. Use versioned migrate tokens to ensure no double-free.

Rollout plan and safety gates:
- Feature flag: kv-tiering-v2 with subflags for pinned promotions, prefetching, dma-bw-limit.
- Canary: 5% of traffic on dedicated canary hosts with increased logging. Observe p50/p95/p99 latency, dma.bandwidth_mib_s, and host-mem-pressure for 48 hrs.
- Abort criteria: p99 increase >10% vs baseline OR sustained dma_bandwidth > configured limit for 15 minutes OR host pinned > 2x expected target for 30 minutes.

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide: 
- Exact promotion_threshold: what EWMA window balances adaptivity vs oscillation? (experiment: compare 250ms, 1s, 5s windows)
- Should we prioritize pinned space by route importance (SLA) rather than pure frequency? This complicates accounting but could improve latency for high-value customers.
- Implementation portability: systems without real UMA/zero-copy support need a no-op path; how to simulate pinned behavior?

Next steps (action items):
- [Marcus] finish synthetic trace harness and run full matrix of pinned_fraction_target x dma_max_outstanding by 2025-02-07 (ticket: JIRA-RI-1189).
- [Evelyn] add telemetry for dma.avg_latency_us and kv.pinned_hit_rate in the console panel by 2025-01-31.
- [Ravi] prototype batch-DMA coalescing and submit a small PR for DMA queue bookkeeping (PR linked above).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas to try later:
- Adaptive pinned_fraction_target that grows with observed reuse in the last N seconds but decays slowly to free pinned memory after load spikes.
- Cross-tenant fairness: a weighted token-bucket for DMA issuing.
- Use hardware page migration features (when available) to move pages without copying in future kernel/driver updates.

Summary:
A three-tier KV residency policy (GPU / host-pinned / host-pageable) with conservative promotion and bounded prefetching shows promising tradeoffs in early experiments: significant reduction in p99 latency at modest host-memory cost and much lower PCIe bandwidth usage compared to naive pageable-only designs. The next priority is robust telemetry, a safe canary rollout, and further tuning of promotion windows to avoid oscillation.
